scope.execution: static review informed by existing run evidence; tests were not run

performance_metrics.playwright_parallelism: fullyParallel enabled; 4 local workers; 1 CI worker

observations.assessment: Seven E2E cases each navigate once. This is expected per-test browser isolation, and the measured three-round wall time does not indicate excessive reload cost.
Fresh in-memory DemoStore instances use a tiny fixed fixture and preserve test isolation. They are necessary independent SQLite state and are not reported as slow setup.

The concurrency contract test creates 64 bounded short-lived threads once to exercise simultaneous correlation-ID allocation. With the existing Rust suite pass evidence and no repeated setup loop, this is not a performance violation.
Two tests launch one child test process each to capture redacted stderr/output or isolate Windows Credential Manager behavior. Process boundaries are required by those assertions and are bounded.
CI uses one Playwright worker while local runs use four. This is a conservative stability setting, not a violation on current evidence; increase only after CI resource and flake data support it.

recommendations: Keep the current four-worker local Playwright setting and fullyParallel mode.
Retain per-test in-memory SQLite isolation; optimize only if future timing evidence identifies database setup as a bottleneck.
Track CI Playwright duration over time and cautiously raise CI workers only when runner capacity and flake history justify it.
summary: No performance violations found. The suite uses parallel execution where supported, has no hard waits or unnecessary serial groups, and existing 49/49 Rust, 19/19 Vitest, 7/7 Playwright plus 21/21 burn-in evidence supports the current bounded setup costs.
